data: Iscrizioni, epigrafi ed epigrammi in Greco della Sicilia orientale di epoca romana
Giacomo Manganaro, «Iscrizioni, epigrafi ed epigrammi in Greco della Sicilia orientale di epoca romana», Mélanges de l’École Francaise de Rome: Antiquité 106, fasc. 1 (1994): 79–118
Limestone cippus of slightly irregular form.
Text laid out over 18 lines, with a pair of large hederae below
Lunate sigma and epsilon; alpha, mu, delta and lamda with extended upper strokes; uncial omega

Found 'in un fondo in zona di Acata (Ragusa)', prior to 1986 when it was acquired by the Museo Archeologico Regionale Paolo Orsi (according to Manganaro 1994); but not since located there, and perhaps transferred to Ragusa museum?

An outstanding collection of archaeological material. The collection ranges from Siracusa and the surrounding territory (Megara Hyblaia, Akrai, Kasmenai etc) to encompass all of eastern Sicily, reaching as far as Gela and Agrigento. The ground floor covers prehistory through to the end of the Classical period. Upstairs includes Hellenistic and Roman Syracuse and a display of material from the catacombs. A gallery displaying material from Hellenistic eastern Sicily is in preparation.

  • Text of Manganaro 1994

Italian translation

Qui chi (e')? Montano medico e agricoltore ventottenne giacque giovane, la legittima sposa lasciando anzitempo e piccoli figli e i genitori in lamento, che si strappano i canuti capelli, per il fatto che a lui la barba bella cresciuta da poco, di lui che spirava l'anima, tagliarono tra le lacrime. Montano il padre per pieta' ha fatto (la tomba) [trans. G. Manganaro]
